clue.text: Ice age shows old, originally pointless intention

indicators.note: done originally means done in a new, inventive way, so these fourteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news item about some ice age display revealing an old, purposeless plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like it goes with 'pointless', but it is the anagram signal working on all of ICE AGE SHOWS OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild goose chase is a futile pursuit, an aim that can never be achieved, hence an idiom for a pointless undertaking.

clue.text: My boss comes from fantastic town in Scotland

indicators.note: the boss coming out of the word means those letters are taken away from it

parts.note: wicked is slang for excellent or fantastic
the setter's boss is the editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their boss hails from a wonderful Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossword setter's boss is the editor, ED. Wick is a town in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Wick is a real town on the north-east coast of Scotland, the county town of Caithness.

clue.text: Strange being without a legal right to hold property

indicators.note: being without the letter means it is removed from the word

parts.note: an alien is a strange creature from elsewhere

explanation.surface: Someone odd finds themselves lacking any legal claim to keep possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is the legal right to keep another person's property until a debt is settled.

clue.text: Horse in German producing dad joke!

indicators.note: the horse is placed in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat of mixed colour

explanation.surface: A German horse somehow comes out with a terrible pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A groaner is a pun or joke so weak that it makes listeners groan, exactly what a dad joke does.

clue.text: Adored rocking up, grasping instruction

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the hidden letters run backwards
the words hold the answer inside them, as if grasped

explanation.surface: A beloved rocking cradle is held while someone gives a command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' looks like an anagram signal but it is just part of the hidden text: ADOREDROCKING holds REDRO, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is a command or instruction someone must follow.

clue.text: Using European vote yet to be decided

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper
pending means not yet settled

explanation.surface: A European ballot whose outcome is still undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: Expending something means using it up, spending it, as with energy or money.

clue.text: See 1
Hurtful piece taken out of paper

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a press ..., an article clipped from a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a nasty newspaper article; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark can be cutting, that is wounding, and a clipped newspaper article is called a cutting.

clue.text: A model felt in charge, having a tone likely to scare many off

definitions.text: having a tone likely to scare many off

parts.note: to model is to pose for an artist
felt is matted fibre, and to felt is to mat together

explanation.surface: An artist's model in charge, speaking in a tone that frightens people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tone' here means colouring, not voice: the answer is a zoological term.
explanation.definitionFit: Aposematic colouring is the bright warning colouration of creatures like wasps, which deters predators from attacking.

clue.text: Watch at an end then — till he begs for a change

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene of someone pleading over a watch until its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece, but it is a sailor's shift on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: On board ship, eight bells is rung at the close of each four-hour duty period, marking its finish.

clue.text: Cardinal must be fixed in firm belief

indicators.note: the colour is set inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
cardinal is a deep red colour

explanation.surface: A churchman, a cardinal, must stay firmly settled in his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but here it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or set of principles someone holds.

clue.text: Strip after swim — hot feature of 28!

indicators.note: the strip comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a thong is a narrow strip of leather, or skimpy garment

explanation.surface: Changing into a skimpy thong after a dip on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is EIDER, whose opening EI is a gliding vowel sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A diphthong is a vowel sound that glides from one quality to another, as in the opening of the duck's name.

clue.text: Not willing to compromise en route, absorbing information

indicators.note: the information is taken inside the phrase

parts.note: in transit means on the way
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A stubborn traveller refuses to budge while taking in information on the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An intransigent person is stubborn and refuses to change their views or reach agreement.

clue.text: Redesigned estate surrounding market to fit together perfectly

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the market word
a redesign reworks the letters into a new order

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A housing estate is remodelled around a market so everything fits neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapes that tessellate interlock to cover a surface with no gaps or overlaps, like tiles.

clue.text: Strange promise, keeping left for a better place than ours

parts.note: other can mean different or strange

indicators.note: the promise holds the letter inside

parts.note: giving your word is making a promise

explanation.surface: An odd vow made while hoping for a paradise beyond this life.
explanation.definitionFit: The otherworld is a spiritual realm or afterlife, imagined as superior to earthly existence.

clue.text: Medical speciality I'm not sure I caught — this is to do with the guts

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
er is a hesitant interjection
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A doctor unsure whether they've caught some digestive bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric means relating to the intestines, as in enteric fever.

clue.text: Conservative moving cheaply saving time for this way!

indicators.note: the reworked letters keep the time letter inside them
moving the letters around rearranges them

explanation.surface: A Tory travelling on the cheap and saving time picks this route.
explanation.walkthrough: A bicycle is the cheap, time-saving way to travel, which is what the surface hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle path is a route set aside for bicycles, a kind of way or track.

clue.text: Such a person won't welcome home fire here!

parts.note: in means at home
a grate is where a fire burns

explanation.surface: A grumpy figure who refuses any welcome by the fireside at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, someone who shows no thanks for kindness received.

clue.text: Local that you'll find in frenzy online

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pub, the local, is caught up in an internet frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a pub but means regional or dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is a dialect or archaic word for that, as in yon hill.

clue.text: One who might scoff being infected, catching cold

indicators.note: the infected word catches the letter inside it

parts.note: septic means infected

explanation.surface: Someone with an infected wound who also catches a chill and mocks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts claims, and so may sneer or mock at them.

clue.text: Instructor's riddle with no end of stress

indicators.note: having none of that letter means it is removed

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, a strainer

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher's puzzle that never lets up on stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' is a puzzle in the surface but a sieve here; dropping the S that ends 'stress' leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a coach who teaches skills to people or animals.

clue.text: Hostile American agents left after golf, oddly

indicators.note: the American pieces come after the golf letters
taking the odd-placed letters of the word

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Spies from the US leave unfriendly after a strange round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial manner is icy and unfriendly, figuratively cold.

clue.text: Amount of land and time needed to billet most of elite

indicators.note: billeting means lodging, so the time houses the trimmed word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: How much land and time it takes to lodge most of an elite force.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area of land measured in acres.

clue.text: Greatest point of degradation in raw metalwork, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Some crude metalwork represents the worst state of decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-water mark is the lowest level something reaches, figuratively its worst state.

clue.text: Comes across suitable applicants at last

parts.note: meet is an archaic word for fitting or suitable

indicators.note: take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recruiter finally encounters some suitable job applicants.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to encounter them, come across them.

clue.text: Independent party lifted holiday island

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: LAB is short for Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: An independent group raises funds for a holiday on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with tourists.

clue.text: Comfortable with arms raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards

parts.note: arms are weapons, guns

explanation.surface: Someone at ease with their arms lifted, perhaps stretching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' are limbs in the surface but weapons here.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means cosy and comfortable.

clue.text: Endlessly drying clutch valve in engine

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: airing clothes is drying them
to take is to grasp or clutch

explanation.surface: A mechanic describing an engine's clutch and valve parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutch' and 'valve' suggest car parts, but clutch is a verb meaning grab.
explanation.definitionFit: An air intake is the opening through which an engine draws in air, sometimes controlled by a valve.

clue.text: Once more a short answer must be accepted

indicators.note: the drink accepts the letter inside it

parts.note: a short is a measure of spirits such as gin

explanation.surface: A brief reply that has to be taken repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it shortens 'answer', but it is the drink: a short is a small serving of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, a repetition.

clue.text: Senior member will need one for large flier

indicators.note: the senior word will need a replacement letter put in
for means in place of, so one letter swaps out the other

parts.note: an elder is a senior member of a church or community
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A senior committee member needs someone to stand in for a big flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, a bird, hence something that flies.

clue.text: Imposing a penalty, having dropped starter in a rush

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: chastening means punishing or disciplining

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly hands out a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastening means hurrying or moving quickly.
